let-the-barbarians-in.summary: Peter Bauman, Le Random’s editor in chief, attended Art Basel, Basel 2026 and its various side events and exhibitions. He connects his thoughts and a mini-diary to the discussion surrounding the Art Basel talk, “Barbarians at the Gate," with Tina Rivers Ryan, Trevor Paglen, Erick Calderon and Natasha Degen. Bauman suggests that the Zero 10 digital sector and anti-fair Basel Social Club are less barbarians than civilized "Normans," challenging the status quo but ultimately part of the institutional art world. The true "barbarians" are the general public who currently feel excluded from art spaces, emphasizing that the industry must produce work and find sustainable economic models to engage them.

They cover the origin and evolution of Carl Thoma's collecting instincts as well as Thoma Foundation's collecting thesis and loan philosophy for Digital & Media Art. They close by discussing the art-historical framing of Rozin's Interference. The Carl & Marilynn Thoma Art Foundation stewards a 1,700+ work collection spanning Art of the Spanish Americas, Digital & Media Art, Japanese Bamboo and Post-war Painting & Sculpture. It supports the field through loans, research, exhibitions, conservation and over $26 million in grants since its founding in 2014.

The LACMA work, SPIRITS, consists of live 3D sculptures of sandals and shoes from beaches across the world. The project culminates on June 21, 2026, with a summer solstice dance at LACMA featuring Richie Hawtin. They cover gerrard's twenty-year arc from early game engine works to browser-based public art; the entanglement of petroleum, plasticity, and modern life; and why gerrard believes the game engine is the most important medium of our time.

Elliott is exhibiting two dozen works at the forefront of creativity and AI on-site at Denver's Colorado Convention Center (June 5–7, 2026) and 114 online at the CVPR 2026 Art Gallery. The curator speaks with three shortlisted artists about their creative and conceptual approaches to AI: Nick Oh & Alex Park, Avital Meshi & Dorte Bjerre Jensen, and Xia Liu.

The artist spoke with Peter Bauman (Monk Antony) about her accidental path to painting and the recent integration of custom AI workflows into her practice. They discuss slop aesthetics, the dopamine blowout of contemporary image consumption, and how Baudrillard's theories of spectacle inform Singer’s long use of technology to interrogate the changing nature of image production.

Peter Bauman argues protocol art and worldbuilding externalize the brain’s two halves: the protocolic urge to formalize reality into rules and the worlding urge to inhabit it as an open, living environment.

Fujimoto is exhibiting at Personal Structures in Palazzo Mora alongside the Venice Biennale (May 9–November 22, 2026).

They cover her path from ceramic sculpture to analog video with Phil Morton to real-time computer animation. Veeder's interactive experiments on the Zgrass machine's repurposed video game hardware anticipated by decades the game-engine-driven world-building that now anchors major museum collections and biennials.

living-aesthetics-a-grammar-of-protocol-.summary: Protocol artist and theorist Primavera De Filippi and Peter Bauman (Monk Antony) trace art's route to life through its grammar. They map how artists make work as, with and about protocols and worlds, which arise when rules shift from the first person to the third.

a-a-murakami-on-existence-as-medium.summary: Artist duo A.A.Murakami spoke with Peter Bauman (Monk Antony) about creating screenless immersive art and technology installations, where existence itself is the medium. Their solo exhibition New Nature opens September 1, 2026 at Paradise City Art Gallery, Seoul.

lowbie-and-duc-de-berry-on-log-and-the-n.summary: Artists Lowbie and Duc de Berry discuss the origins of LOG, their small-batch art zine, with VVV. They cover the zine tradition, the NFT-to-zine pipeline, curating a scene and why two artists who live online turned to print.

john-provencher-and-raster-on-generative.summary: Artist John Provencher joins Raster’s founders, thefunnyguys and Michael Elsdoerfer, to discuss collaborating on the generative system, Raster Logo. With Peter Bauman (Monk Antony), they cover the bitmap wordmark at the system's core, the inspiration for a generative logo and what Raster's founders make of the platform's first year.

agnieszka-kurant-on-alien-thoughts.author: Peter Bauman
agnieszka-kurant-on-alien-thoughts.summary: Multidisciplinary artificial life artist Agnieszka Kurant recently participated in two shows alongside the Venice Biennale, Rhizome’s Seven on Seven in New York and Zero 10 in Basel during Art Basel. The artist spoke with Peter Bauman (Monk Antony). They discuss how the shows align with her radically experimental and collaborative views on systems of collective intelligence, including alien thoughts and wordless conversations.
